hooks.text: "Hotels hire me to make their spaces look inevitable. Most of them have no idea what that actually takes."
hooks.rationale: Models the contrarian hot-take pattern that drove 2.16x and 2.51x multipliers for @juliabroome this cycle. It creates tension by implying a gap between client expectation and the craft behind the work. Natalie's Forbes Five-Star training gives her the standing to own this claim without it reading as arrogant.

hooks.text: "POV: 6am, a suite no one has slept in yet, and the light is doing something I have never seen before."
hooks.rationale: Directly models the scene-setting POV format behind @rocioprezg's 2.90x hotel-opening reel — the highest multiplier from a hospitality photographer this cycle. Sensory and time-specific, it sells access and presence without naming a property, making it reusable across shoots. Fits Natalie's natural-light pillar precisely.

hooks.text: "The England most people never see — a Cotswolds garden in the hour before guests arrive."
hooks.rationale: Adapts the named-place curiosity-gap formula from @jameslloydcole's 2.39x Gresgarth Hall post, which consistently beat his scenic location content. Layering a specific geography with a restricted time window creates aspiration and access signal in a single line. Natalie's London residency plan makes UK hospitality content a natural on-brand extension.
